text:
Alice C: Hey team — I'm in my first week and trying to access the 'team-a' namespace with a service account. I created a serviceaccount alice-sa in team-a, but when I switch context I get: "Error from server (Unauthorized): You must be logged in to the server". Anyone point me to the standard way we provision kubeconfigs for SAs? Do I need a secret/token or use impersonation? Thanks!

Priya G: Welcome Alice :tada: Quick q — are you trying to use the SA secret token or impersonation? We usually avoid long-lived SA secrets; infra prefers short-lived tokens or impersonation. If you're blocked, you can create a namespace-scoped Role + RoleBinding and use the SA token for now.

Mark L: For a quick workaround, get the token with:
```
kubectl -n team-a get sa alice-sa -o jsonpath='{.secrets[0].name}'
kubectl -n team-a get secret <secret-name> -o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 -d
```
Then add to kubeconfig:
```
kubectl config set-credentials alice-sa-token --token="<TOKEN>"
kubectl config set-context alice-sa --cluster=redwood-cluster --namespace=team-a --user=alice-sa-token
kubectl config use-context alice-sa
```
But make sure the SA actually has a RoleBinding for whatever verbs you need.

Priya G: Prefer this instead (sa + role binding):
```
kubectl create role app-reader --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods,services -n team-a
kubectl create rolebinding alice-sa-reader --role=app-reader --serviceaccount=team-a:alice-sa -n team-a
```
Then use the token approach above.

Alice C: I tried grabbing the secret but the SA shows no secrets (secretName empty). Is that because automountServiceAccountToken is off by default? Any idea?

Mark L: If the SA has automount disabled, there won't be a secret. On newer clusters you can create a token directly with the TokenRequest API. Easiest: 
```
kubectl -n team-a create token alice-sa --duration=1h
```
That prints a token you can copy into kubeconfig.

infra-bot: Heads-up: please don't create cluster-admin bindings. For elevated access, open an infra ticket requesting temporary elevation and include the API actions you need.

Priya G: Also, if you're on EKS/GKE, it's preferable to use the cloud provider's token flow (e.g. `aws eks get-token` / `gcloud container clusters get-credentials`) rather than long-lived SA tokens. But `kubectl create token` is fine for short test sessions.

Alice C: Awesome — `kubectl create token alice-sa --duration=2h` fixed it. I added the credential to my kubeconfig and can list pods in team-a now. Thanks everyone!

Priya G: Nice! If you want, file a quick request in #eng-infra to have a permanent RoleBinding created for alice-sa instead of relying on manual tokens. Also welcome aboard :wave:

Alice C: Thanks — filing that ticket now and excited to be here!
